nodes.summary: It is not the case that the complement of every Sidon set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ contains an infinite arithmetic progression: there is a Sidon set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that for all natural numbers $a$ and $d \ge 1$ some term $a + kd$, $k \in \mathbb{N}$, lies in $A$. Here $A$ is Sidon when $w + x = y + z$ with $w, x, y, z \in A$ forces $\{w, x\} = \{y, z\}$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 198 is false

nodes.summary: The proposition that the complement of every Sidon set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ contains an infinite arithmetic progression: for every Sidon set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ there are natural numbers $a$ and $d \ge 1$ such that $a + kd \notin A$ for every natural number $k$.
